steps.description: Issue Section 94 BNSS notices to TSPs to trace mobile numbers linked to the publisher account KYC or numbers used by individuals conducting secondary phone harassment/threats against the victim. Demand CAF, CDR with tower locations, and IMEI histories.
required_evidence: CAF and CDR with Cell ID locations for phone numbers linked to the publisher handle or secondary harassers
IMEI tracking history establishing device ownership and physical movement patterns
Call analysis establishing links between online publishers and offline stalking/harassment suspects
steps.condition_to_start: Phone numbers identified from platform KYC or victim's incoming harassment call logs.
steps.condition_to_complete: Receipt of CAF, CDR, and IMEI data confirming suspect identities and physical locations.
if_blocked: If secondary harassment calls originate from bulk VOIP numbers, coordinate with DoT TERM cell to trace the gateway switch and block the trunk line.

steps.title: Search, Seizure of Electronic Devices & Arrest of Doxxer
steps.description: Execute search warrants at the physical residence or workplace of the identified doxxer. Arrest the suspect and seize computers, laptops, mobile phones, and storage media. Perform forensic imaging to recover local copies of the victim's private data, compiling logs, and publishing scripts.
required_evidence: Seizure memos of computing devices, mobile phones, and storage media
Forensic bit-stream images of seized hardware containing stored victim private data, forum login tokens, and publishing histories
Arrest memos and interrogation disclosures detailing motive (revenge, political targeting, extortion)
steps.condition_to_start: Actionable physical address established from ISP, telecom, or platform tracing.
steps.condition_to_complete: Arrest of doxxing culprit, physical seizure of hardware, and submission of digital exhibits to FSL.
if_blocked: If the doxxer is an offline acquaintance, employee, or rival operating locally, cross-reference handset IMEI histories and Wi-Fi logs with known local suspects.

steps.title: Judicial Filing, Permanent Injunction & Restraining Orders
steps.description: File the comprehensive forensic chargesheet before the jurisdictional Magistrate under IT Act Section 66E (Privacy Violation) and relevant BNS defamation/harassment sections. Obtain a formal judicial injunction restraining the accused from publishing or disseminating any private personal data of the victim permanently.
required_evidence: Certified FSL scientific analysis report linking seized devices to the online publication of doxxed data
Section 63 BSA electronic certificates for all intermediary, ISP, and telecom records
Judicial order granting permanent privacy injunctions and ordering destruction of seized copies of victim's personal data
steps.condition_to_start: Investigation finalized, accused arrested, and FSL reports received.
steps.condition_to_complete: Charge-sheet accepted by court and formal privacy restraining/injunction orders issued.
if_blocked: If doxxed data continues to circulate on third-party scraper websites, serve the certified judicial injunction order on hosting providers and domain registrars globally to mandate takedown.

dead_end_strategies.condition: Doxxing was executed by anonymous online mobs or activist hacktivists using offshore paste sites and TOR networks with no persistent domestic IP or telecom trail.
suggested_actions: Prioritize victim physical security and digital damage control: assist the victim in changing phone numbers, flagging compromised bank accounts/IDs, and requesting removal from data broker registries.
Maintain automated monitoring on search engines and major social media platforms; submit continuous de-indexing and takedown requests for any newly appearing URLs hosting the doxxed dossier.

Examine the offline source of the leaked data (e.g., how the private address or document was originally acquired) to investigate potential physical breaches, stolen mail, or unauthorized database access by institutions.

crime_type: Reporting & Escalation of Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) Encountered Online
title: Standard Operating Procedure for Procedural Escalation, Reporting & Evidence Preservation of Online CSAM
source: Synthesized from POCSO Act Section 19/20 guidelines, IT Rules 2021 (Rule 3(2)(c)), NCRP CSAM SOPs, and MHA directives

steps.title: Strict Evidentiary Containment & Hash Logging (No Copying Rule)
steps.description: Upon encountering or receiving reports of online CSAM, strictly adhere to statutory containment protocols: DO NOT download, save, forward, or create local copies of the illicit files on personal or station computers to avoid secondary transmission offenses under POCSO/IT Act. Document ONLY the exact URLs, platform identifiers, timestamps, and generate/record SHA-256 cryptographic hashes of the file streams directly in write-blocked investigative logs.
required_evidence: Exact URLs, web links, or platform container identifiers hosting the illicit material
SHA-256 / MD5 cryptographic hash values of the offending media files recorded in official case diary
Investigating Officer's statutory containment certification confirming no unauthorized local copying or transmission occurred
Screenshot of platform container metadata (excluding descriptive depiction of illicit content)
steps.legal_basis: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act Section 20
steps.condition_to_start: Police officer, complainant, or intermediary identifies or reports online CSAM or child exploitation material.
steps.condition_to_complete: Exact URLs, timestamps, and file hashes documented in case diary without creating or transmitting local media copies.
if_blocked: If a complainant brings a physical memory card or phone containing CSAM to the police station, immediately seal the device in a tamper-evident forensic bag under seizure memo without viewing or copying, and transfer directly to FSL.

steps.title: Emergency Escalation via NCRP CSAM Portal & I4C Notification
steps.description: Immediately log and escalate the incident onto the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP / cybercrime.gov.in) under the dedicated 'Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) / Rape / Gang Rape (RGR)' reporting mechanism. Transmit the recorded URLs, timestamps, and hash values directly to the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) and the State Cyber Cell / CID for centralized statutory tracking and NCMEC (National Center for Missing & Exploited Children) CyberTipline coordination.
required_evidence: NCRP / CFCFRMS CSAM Ticket Acknowledgement Number
Official transmission dispatch note forwarding IOCs and hash lists to I4C and State Cyber CID
Confirmation receipt from State Cyber Crime Nodal Officer
steps.condition_to_start: URLs, container metadata, and file hashes documented in initial containment log.
steps.condition_to_complete: Incident successfully registered on NCRP CSAM portal and formally acknowledged by I4C / State Cyber CID.
if_blocked: If the online reporting portal is temporarily inaccessible, immediately dispatch an emergency encrypted flash message to the Superintendent of Police (Cyber Crime) and Director I4C via official police communication networks.

steps.title: Mandatory Platform Preservation & Immediate Takedown Requisition
steps.description: Issue statutory emergency notices under IT Rules 2021 (Rule 3(2)(c)) and IT Act Section 79 to online intermediaries (Meta, Google, Telegram, X, cloud storage providers) mandating the immediate removal/disabling of access to the CSAM within 24 hours. Concurrently issue binding Section 94 BNSS notices directing the intermediary to preserve all associated backend data (uploader accounts, IP logs, timestamps) for 180 days for evidentiary purposes.
required_evidence: Written statutory preservation order under BNSS Section 94 / IT Rules served on the intermediary
Intermediary written acknowledgment confirming content removal within 24 hours and preservation of backend logs
Cryptographic hash submission confirmation for cross-platform PhotoDNA blacklist databases
steps.condition_to_start: URLs, container IDs, and hosting platforms identified during initial logging.
steps.condition_to_complete: Intermediary confirms removal of illicit access within 24 hours and confirms statutory preservation of uploader evidence.
if_blocked: If content is hosted on independent overseas servers or darkweb repositories, route emergency blocking orders through CERT-In under entity_id cert_in for nationwide ISP domain blocking.

steps.title: Mandatory CWC Notification & Statutory Child Protection Referral
steps.description: In strict accordance with POCSO Act Section 19 and JJ Act Section 31, formally notify the local Child Welfare Committee (CWC) and the designated Child Welfare Police Officer (CWPO) within 24 hours of recording the CSAM report. If the child victim depicted in the material is identified or suspected to be within the local jurisdiction, coordinate immediate child-protective intervention, medical examination, and support without compromising victim confidentiality.
required_evidence: Formal written statutory notification dispatched to the Child Welfare Committee (CWC) within 24 hours
Entry log of case assignment to the designated Child Welfare Police Officer (CWPO)
CWC proceedings acknowledgment and victim protection directive (if local victim is identified)
steps.legal_basis: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act Section 19
steps.condition_to_start: CSAM incident logged and initial jurisdictional assessment initiated.
steps.condition_to_complete: Statutory 24-hour CWC notification requirement fulfilled and child protection protocols initiated.
if_blocked: If CWC formal sittings are not in session, serve the mandatory statutory notification directly to the Chairperson or Member residing in the district via registered electronic/physical dispatch.

steps.title: Requisition of Uploader Account KYC & Technical Access Logs
steps.description: Issue Section 94 BNSS notices to the hosting platforms, social media intermediaries, or cloud storage providers where the CSAM was uploaded or shared. Demand complete subscriber registration KYC, verified mobile numbers, linked email addresses, upload IP addresses with exact UTC/IST timestamps, and account login histories.
required_evidence: Subscriber registration details, verified mobile numbers, and recovery email IDs of the uploader handle
Exact upload and login IP addresses with synchronized timestamps (down to seconds) and source port numbers
Platform audit logs showing account sharing history, group dissemination, or associated device user-agents
steps.condition_to_start: Intermediary confirms preservation of uploader backend data.
steps.condition_to_complete: Receipt of complete subscriber KYC and technical upload IP logs from the intermediary.
if_blocked: If uploader accounts utilize foreign web services (e.g., Google Drive, Mega.nz), serve notices under entity_id google_llc for subscriber metadata while routing international preservation through I4C.

steps.title: ISP IPDR Resolution & Telecom Subscriber Tracing
steps.description: Analyse the upload IP addresses and source ports obtained from platform logs, as well as any mobile numbers linked to uploader KYC. Issue Section 94 BNSS notices to Internet Service Providers and Telecom Service Providers to obtain IPDR NAT port binding records, CAF dossiers, CDRs, and physical installation addresses of the uploading subscriber.
required_evidence: IPDR logs resolving public upload IPs and NAT source ports to specific private subscriber installation addresses
ISP subscriber KYC showing physical residential/commercial premises of the uploader
CAF and CDR with Cell ID locations for any telecom mobile numbers linked to the uploading account
IMEI tracking history establishing hardware device identity
steps.condition_to_start: Actionable upload IP addresses, source ports, or mobile numbers obtained from intermediary logs.
steps.condition_to_complete: Positive identification of the ISP/Telecom subscriber name and exact physical residential/workplace address.
if_blocked: If IP addresses resolve to mobile data networks, route IPDR and tower dump requisitions through entity_id telecom_operator.

steps.title: Specialized Tactical Raid, Hardware Seizure & Forensic Triage
steps.description: Execute coordinated search and seizure warrants at the physical premises identified via ISP and telecom tracing, led by an officer not below the rank of Sub-Inspector (preferably accompanied by CWPO/female officers). Arrest the suspect. Seize all computing devices, mobile phones, routers, storage media, and cameras. Perform on-site live forensic containment to ensure write-protection of storage drives without viewing or copying media locally.
required_evidence: Seizure memos of computers, laptops, mobile phones, hard drives, USB drives, and routers executed under strict chain of custody
Tamper-evident forensic seal certifications for all seized hardware items
Arrest memos and statutory interrogation records (strictly avoiding unnecessary verbal description of illicit media)
Forwarding dispatch letter sending seized sealed hardware directly to State FSL / CFSL for forensic extraction
steps.condition_to_start: Actionable physical premises and subscriber identity established from ISP or telecom tracing.
steps.condition_to_complete: Arrest of suspect, physical seizure of hardware under write-protected seals, and secure transfer of exhibits to FSL.
if_blocked: If the suspect attempts to trigger remote wipe or destroy hardware upon police entry, immediately isolate devices in Faraday bags and disconnect power/battery interfaces.

steps.title: Sealed Judicial Filing, Statutory Custody & Evidence Disposal Orders
steps.description: Compile the FSL scientific analysis report (confirming cryptographic hash matches of CSAM on seized hardware), Section 63 BSA certificates, and procedural logs into a sealed charge-sheet. File the prosecution report before the Special POCSO Court / Magistrate under IT Act Sections 67B and relevant POCSO provisions. Move statutory applications under BNSS to ensure all digital CSAM exhibits remain in sealed judicial custody throughout trial and obtain binding judicial orders mandating permanent forensic destruction of all illicit media upon case conclusion.
required_evidence: Certified FSL scientific analysis report confirming cryptographic hash matches of CSAM on seized accused devices (submitted in sealed cover)
Section 63 BSA electronic certificates for all intermediary, ISP, and NCRP portal records
Final sealed police charge-sheet filed before the Special POCSO Court / Magistrate
Judicial order directing sealed trial proceedings and permanent post-trial forensic destruction of all illicit digital exhibits
steps.legal_basis: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act Section 24
steps.condition_to_start: Investigation finalized, accused arrested, and sealed FSL hash-verification reports received.
steps.condition_to_complete: Sealed charge-sheet accepted by Special POCSO Court and mandatory judicial evidence-destruction/privacy orders issued.
if_blocked: If defense counsel seeks physical or digital copies of the CSAM exhibits for inspection, strongly oppose reproduction under POCSO Section 20 / BNSS, requesting the court to permit supervised viewing only within sealed court premises without copying.

dead_end_strategies.condition: CSAM upload originated from an anonymized foreign IP address or darkweb node (.onion) utilizing offshore bulletproof hosting with no actionable domestic Indian subscriber or telecom footprint.
suggested_actions: Transmit all identified cryptographic file hashes, container URLs, and technical IOCs immediately to I4C, CERT-In, and INTERPOL / NCMEC CyberTipline for global international database syndication and server takedown.

Ensure permanent domestic containment by verifying that all identified URLs, domains, and hash strings are integrated into national ISP blocking filters and intermediary PhotoDNA rejection lists via MeitY orders.
Close the domestic procedural log with a formal statutory report to the Child Welfare Committee (CWC) and Special Court documenting that international mitigation protocols have been fully activated.
